about: Touched-path → test-suite map (bothouse#236), read by `botq test-map`. The acceptance gate derives every landed job's touched paths from its own diff and requires the commands mapped here green — independent of the job's brief. First matching rule wins: specific rules above broad ones. `tests: []` means CONSCIOUSLY untested and must carry its why. An unmapped path fails the resolver loud. Commands run from the repo root; lint completeness with `botq test-map --check`.

rules.why: editing the map re-lints its own completeness over every tracked file, and the guard test pins the landing-matrix commands so a config cannot be silently dropped from the rule below (--check lints completeness, not content)
prose, licenses, and evidence artifacts (screenshots/logs recorded under docs/evidence)
CI workflow definitions — exercised only by dispatching them on GitHub Actions; no local runner exists, and a broken workflow fails loudly at dispatch
operator tooling (profiling, terrain bake, asset fetch) and live proof scripts — exercised by use against a running system, no offline harness

the browser build/serve/verify/deploy harness (rl#411 stages 5-6) — a live harness exercised by RUNNING run.sh (verify drives headless chromium; deploy.sh pushes to live hosting; no offline harness); shellcheck + node syntax checks keep it mechanically sound, and game-web/src/ rides the general rust rule below

the browser↔native cross-play formation probe (rl#412) — a live-network canary exercised by RUNNING run.sh against the n0 relays (no offline harness; form_web.rs rides the general rust rule from net/examples/); shellcheck keeps the runner mechanically sound

the browser↔native relay echo probe (rl#411 stage 4) — a live-network canary exercised by RUNNING run.sh against the n0 relays (no offline harness; its .rs halves ride the general rust rule from net-link/examples/); shellcheck keeps the runner mechanically sound
the pinned dev environment — every mapped suite below runs inside it, so a break fails those commands loudly

tests: nix-shell --run 'cargo check --target wasm32-unknown-unknown -p net-proto -p net-link -p game-web'
rules.why: the chase-eval measurement seam (rl#341 S2-5): the physical path — run_eval through real batched bevy+rapier worlds, the fold, every guard — had ZERO executed coverage because its only end-to-end test is #[ignore]d (too heavy for every workspace change). First-match-wins shadows the general rust rule, so this rule carries the full landing matrix PLUS the --ignored end-to-end run (release, ~1 min after kache-warm compile); a regression in the settle/active split, the running min, the rescue forfeit, or the batched env wiring now fails a landing that touches the seam

tests: nix-shell --run 'cargo check --target wasm32-unknown-unknown -p net-proto -p net-link -p game-web'
rules.why: AGENTS.md's pre-submission contract, workspace-wide, plus the rl#411 platform-freedom check: net-proto (the protocol core) and net-link (the link layer, rl#411 stage 4 — its web half only compiles on wasm32) and game-web (the browser entry, rl#411 stage 5 — checking it compiles the ENTIRE web leaf: net+crab-world with render on wasm32) must stay wasm32-green, and its wasm build breaks from DEP-side edits too (crab-world, workspace Cargo.toml) — so the check rides the general rule for every rust touch, not a net-proto-scoped one; it is a seconds-cheap cargo check when warm. The crates interlock (net/game consume crab-world's sim seams), so per-crate scoping would miss cross-crate breakage; --test-threads=2 because the live trainer saturates the cores and the heavy physics tests hang at default parallelism; assets and golden data ride the same rule because the suite consumes them (terrain fixtures, golden-env data, controls-display images). The two ISOLATED --release builds are the literal configs rl-release.service ships, which workspace feature-unification MASKS (bothouse#79/#97, formerly botq's hardcoded rl build matrix): `-p rl-train` is the trainer/eval build — default features only (wgpu, no render), where rl#275's ungated `pub use` of render-gated code broke E0432 while every workspace-level build stayed green; `-p rl-demo -p game -p rl-update-ui` is the deck-bundle build — render on WITHOUT the trainer's wgpu, the symmetric unification gap
